newsitem.title: FRANCE: Human rights chief proposed for Council of Europe.
newsitem.headline: Human rights chief proposed for Council of Europe.

text.p: A plan to create the new post of human rights commissioner at the 40-member Council of Europe was endorsed on Monday by Leni Fischer, president of the council's parliamentary assembly.
"This seems to me to be an important idea which should be considered at the autumn summit (of the organisation's heads of government)," Fischer told reporters.
The council aims to protect human rights and democracy.
Its summit is expected to take place in Strasbourg, eastern France, in October. It will help the council prepare for eventual expansion into central and eastern Europe.
Finnish Foreign Minister Tarja Halonen, who currently chairs the council's committee of ministers, first proposed naming a human rights chief.
The individual would be responsible for assuring that judgments of the council's European Court of Human Rights are carried out.
